clean_source_blocks.text: Rescuers spent six hours carefully digging to reach one of the boys, as many residents continue searching through the rubble by hand, still waiting for heavy machinery to arrive.

More than three days after the quakes, rescuers had not given up hope, saying people could still be alive, especially if they had access to food and water under the rubble. The two earthquakes, which struck within 39 seconds, caused hundreds of buildings to collapse and many people remain trapped inside. Desperate families have been digging through the debris by hand, trying to find their loved ones. More than 770 buildings have been partially or completely destroyed and tens of thousands of people remain missing after Venezuela's two earthquakes. (Rueters: Miguel Medina) An infant and two 11-year-old boys pulled alive from underneath rubble are among at least 33 people rescued after Venezuela's two devastating earthquakes. A multinational search and rescue operation continues to sift through heavily impacted areas, while tens of thousands of people remain unaccounted-for. The European Union and the US have announced they will offer emergency assistance and relief packages worth millions to aid the disaster response. Rescuers in Venezuela have saved an infant and two 11-year-old boys from lying underneath rubble caused by Venezuela's devastating earthquakes. The three children are among at least 33 people who were rescued during a weekend multinational operation that continued searching for survivors, while tens of thousands remained unaccounted-for.

An 11-year-old boy, named Moises, was rescued after days trapped beneath heavy rubble Two 11-year-old boys have separately been rescued from the rubble of collapsed buildings within hours of each other, after powerful earthquakes struck Venezuela. Video footage of the first boy, named as Moises, showed him being pulled from the twisted debris - his eyes covered to protect them from the sun - to the applause of rescuers. Hours later, interim President Delcy Rodríquez announced another 11-year-old boy had been rescued, and posted a video of him on X, being carried down a huge mound of wreckage on a stretcher. Since the magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 quakes on Wednesday, officials have confirmed at least 1,450 deaths. Tens of thousands of people are still missing.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
An 11-year-old boy, named Moises, was rescued after days trapped beneath heavy rubble

Two 11-year-old boys have separately been rescued from the rubble of collapsed buildings within hours of each other, after powerful earthquakes struck Venezuela.

Video footage of the first boy, named as Moises, showed him being pulled from the twisted debris - his eyes covered to protect them from the sun - to the applause of rescuers.

Hours later, interim President Delcy Rodríquez announced another 11-year-old boy had been rescued, and posted a video of him on X, being carried down a huge mound of wreckage on a stretcher.

Since the magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 quakes on Wednesday, officials have confirmed at least 1,450 deaths. Tens of thousands of people are still missing.

More than three days after the quakes, rescuers had not given up hope, saying people could still be alive, especially if they had access to food and water under the rubble.

The two earthquakes, which struck within 39 seconds, caused hundreds of buildings to collapse and many people remain trapped inside. Desperate families have been digging through the debris by hand, trying to find their loved ones.

Some have told the BBC that they can hear people under the rubble, but cannot move the heavy slabs of concrete, and are waiting anxiously for heavy machinery to arrive.

11-year-old Moises was pulled out of the rubble after being trapped for days

Colombia's National Unit for Disaster Risk Management (UNGRD) said Moises was buried under about 3m (9.8ft) of debris, and the rescue team spent six hours conducting "high-precision work" on Saturday to reach him.

Reuters reported that a rescuer was overheard on a walkie-talkie saying the young boy was found near his sister and mother, who had both died.

Hours later, Delcy Rodríguez posted a video on X, purportedly showing the rescue of the second 11-year-old boy in the town of Caraballeda.

"In these hours, every life is hope for Venezuela," she wrote.

Officials said the coastal region of La Guaira, where Caraballeda is located, has been hit the hardest.

Rescuers' efforts have been hampered by aftershocks, which are in turn terrifying residents.

"To be honest, it makes you feel kind of nervous. Any little noise... horrible," Jesús Andueza, a 64-year-old bus driver told BBC Mundo.

Thousands of people are living in their cars or camping at places like the airport and golf course, away from buildings that could collapse.

[Lähde: The Mirror]
Two boys are pulled from the rubble of collapsed buildings in quake-hit Venezuela - a glimmer of hope among the devastation that has left 1,430 dead.

Astonishing footage shows the 11-year-olds emerge from the twisted debris of their homes, hours apart. Relieved rescuers erupt in applause as one boy, named Moises, shields his eyes from the sun, four days after the South American country was rocked by a series of powerful quakes.

Hours later, interim President Delcy Rodríquez announced another 11-year-old boy had been rescued. Video posted on social media showed him being carried down a huge mound of wreckage on a stretcher. It purportedly showed the miraculous rescue in the town of Caraballeda. Rodríquez wrote: "In these hours, every life is hope for Venezuela."

It comes after officials confirmed at least 1,430 people had been killed in the back-to-back 7.2 and 7.5-magnitude quakes which hit Wednesday, with at least 68,900 people reported as missing. Towns and villages were reduced to rubble by the strongest shocks since 1900.

The first quake, measured at 7.2 magnitude, struck at 6.04pm local time (11.04pm UK) on Wednesday. That triggered a second reaching 7.5 magnitude 38 seconds later.

The epicentres were 85 miles west of the capital Caracas, but the sheer power of the two shocks caused extensive damage and casualties in the city. payload.title: Kaksi 11-vuotiasta poikaa pelastettiin Venezuelan maanjäristysten raunioista
payload.summary: Venezuelassa kaksi 11-vuotiasta poikaa ja vauva on löydetty elossa raunioista voimakkaiden maanjäristysten jälkeen. Pelastustyöt jatkuvat, ja kymmeniätuhansia ihmisiä on yhä kateissa.
payload.content:
Kaksi 11-vuotiasta poikaa on pelastettu erikseen sortuneiden rakennusten raunioista Venezuelassa useita päiviä voimakkaiden maanjäristysten jälkeen. Viranomaisten mukaan järistykset ovat vaatineet ainakin 1 450 ihmisen hengen, ja kymmeniätuhansia ihmisiä on edelleen kateissa laajoilla tuhoalueilla.

## Lapset löytyivät elossa raunioista

Ensimmäinen pojista on nimetty Moisesiksi. Hänet vedettiin esiin raskaiden raunioiden alta sen jälkeen, kun hän oli ollut loukussa päiviä. Videolla pojan silmät oli peitetty auringonvalolta suojaamiseksi, kun hänet nostettiin pois vääntyneen romun keskeltä pelastajien aplodien saattelemana.

Toinen 11-vuotias poika pelastettiin tunteja myöhemmin. Venezuelan väliaikainen presidentti Delcy Rodríguez kertoi pelastumisesta ja julkaisi videon, jossa poikaa kannettiin paarien päällä alas suurelta rauniokasalta. Myös vauva on löydetty elossa raunioista. Lapset kuuluvat ainakin 33 ihmiseen, jotka pelastettiin viikonlopun aikana jatkuneessa monikansallisessa etsintä- ja pelastusoperaatiossa.

## Rakennuksia sortui sadoittain

Venezuelaa ravisteli keskiviikkona kaksi voimakasta maanjäristystä, joiden magnitudit olivat 7,2 ja 7,5. Järistykset iskivät 39 sekunnin välein. Ne romahduttivat satoja rakennuksia, ja yli 770 rakennusta on tuhoutunut osittain tai kokonaan.

Pelastajat ovat jatkaneet etsintöjä yli kolme päivää järistysten jälkeen, koska heidän mukaansa ihmisiä voi yhä olla hengissä, varsinkin jos heillä on ollut raunioissa ruokaa ja vettä. Yhden pojan tavoittamiseen kului kuusi tuntia varovaista kaivamista.

## Perheet kaivavat käsin

Monet perheet etsivät omaisiaan käsin, sillä raskaita betonilaattoja ei voida siirtää ilman koneita. Osa asukkaista on kertonut kuulevansa ihmisiä raunioiden alta, mutta odottavansa yhä raskaan kaluston saapumista.

Euroopan unioni ja Yhdysvallat ovat ilmoittaneet tarjoavansa hätäapua ja miljoonien arvoisia avustuspaketteja katastrofivasteen tueksi. Monikansallinen etsintä- ja pelastusoperaatio jatkaa työtä pahoin vaurioituneilla alueilla.
summary_bullets: Kaksi 11-vuotiasta poikaa on pelastettu elossa Venezuelan maanjäristysten raunioista.
Ainakin 1 450 ihmisen on vahvistettu kuolleen, ja kymmeniätuhansia on yhä kateissa.
Pelastajat ja asukkaat jatkavat etsintöjä, mutta raskasta kalustoa odotetaan monin paikoin.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu paketin BBC- ja ABC-lähdeotteisiin. Säilytin luvut ja aikamääreet lähteiden mukaisina ja vaihdoin kategorian ulkomaanuutiseksi, koska tapahtuma koskee Venezuelaa.
